speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain. To begin my assessment, please tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if the pain radiates to your arm, jaw, or back.

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture). The history of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption followed by chest pain and choking is classic for this life-threatening esophageal tear. Immediate surgical consultation and imaging are required.
